notes:
=== Weak Service Binary ACL — Service Binary Replacement ===
Overly permissive ACLs on service binaries allow replacement with malicious executable → SYSTEM.

=== DISCOVERY ===
Automated:
  .\SharpUp.exe audit ModifiableServiceBinaries
  (also: PowerUp.ps1 → Invoke-AllChecks)

Manual verification with icacls:
  icacls C:\path\to\service.exe
  Look for: Everyone:(F), BUILTIN\Users:(W), NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users:(W)
  (F) = Full Control, (W) = Write, (M) = Modify — all exploitable

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Identify vulnerable service binary (SharpUp or icacls)
2. Back up original (optional — for client cleanup):
   cp C:\Vuln\Service.exe C:\Vuln\Service.exe.bak
3. Replace with malicious binary:
   cp C:\Tools\shell.exe C:\Vuln\Service.exe
4. Restart service:
   sc stop VulnService
   sc start VulnService
   → Malicious binary executes as SYSTEM

=== WHAT MAKES A BINARY "VULNERABLE" ===
Write access by low-privilege groups (Everyone, Users, Authenticated Users) on:
- The service binary itself
- The directory containing the service binary
(Directory write = can rename original + place malicious file with same name)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Weak binary ACL → replace → SYSTEM shell → LSASS dump → domain escalation
Third-party software (backup agents, monitoring tools) commonly misconfigured this way
SharpUp finds this automatically — run it on every Windows foothold
After SYSTEM: add admin user, deploy persistence, dump credentials

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
BUILTIN\Users or Everyone with write access on anything in Program Files = automatic flag
C:\Windows binaries should never have user-writable ACLs — report immediately
Directory ACL vs file ACL: directory write allows name-substitution attack even without direct file write OSCP Ch16 workflow: Get-CimInstance win32_service → icacls on binary → replace if BUILTIN\Users has (F) → reboot if Auto startup and no stop permission. PowerUp: Get-ModifiableServiceFile. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 16 (Windows Privilege Escalation).

recommended.note: Reconfigure binPath if the binary isn't writable.

name: Weak Permissions - Replace Modifiable Service Binary
description: When a service's executable is writable by your user, overwrite it with a payload and (re)start the service to run it as the service account (often SYSTEM). Keep a copy of the original to restore.

defense.why_it_works: If a service binary has write permissions for non-admin users (Everyone or BUILTIN\Users), the attacker can replace the executable with a malicious binary. On next service start, the malicious binary executes in the service account's security context (often SYSTEM). icacls reveals the permission misconfiguration.
defense.prerequisites: A service binary with write access for non-admin users. Service must be restartable (directly or via system reboot). A replacement malicious binary.
defense.impact: Arbitrary code execution as the service account (SYSTEM or other privileged account) by replacing a writable service binary.
defense.detection: icacls or accesschk on service binaries by standard user. Modification of a service binary file by non-admin (File integrity monitoring, Event 4663). Service binary hash change. Sysmon Event 11: file created in protected service binary path.
defense.artifacts: File modification: service binary modified by non-admin (Event 4663) | Sysmon Event 11: file created in service binary directory | File integrity monitoring alert | Service restarted with new binary
defense.prevention: Enforce file permissions on all service binary directories — only SYSTEM and Administrators should have write access. Audit with accesschk and icacls during security reviews. Enable file integrity monitoring on service binary directories.
defense.misconfiguration: Application installer incorrectly sets service binary permissions to allow Everyone or Users write access. icacls shows: BUILTIN\Users:(I)(F) or (W) on the service binary.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Writable service binary:
icacls 'C:\Program Files\File Monitor\filepermservice.exe'
# BUILTIN\Users:(I)(F) <- full write for all users!

# Exploit:
copy malicious.exe 'C:\Program Files\File Monitor\filepermservice.exe'
sc stop FilePermSvc
sc start FilePermSvc  # executes malicious.exe as SYSTEM
